proof_summary: For \(p=2d+1\) with \(d\) even, Euler’s criterion turns the character matrix modulo \(p\) into the power matrix \(((x_i-y_j)^d)\); a Vandermonde factorization, together with Wilson’s half-factorial identity, shows every factor (including the remaining scalar) is nonzero. For \(d\) odd (equivalently \(p\equiv3\pmod4\)), reindexing by the subgroup of nonzero squares expresses the columns as an odd mixture of commuting skew-symmetric “difference” and symmetric “sum” group-circulants, forcing the determinant to vanish.
